correctness.rationale: The proof independently checks strict branch displacement and switching-endpoint assignment, derives a bijection of every primitive alternating two-cycle to admissible quartic roots, shows H has at most one positive zero so H has at most three distinct roots, and verifies a sharp rational example with exact sign changes. Sign-changing roots are simple, and \(H'(t)=b(1-m(t))\) yields two hyperbolic sinks and one source for F^2. An exact Fraction checker reruns the rational witness; its finite computation is not substituted for the global proof.

value.rationale: Primitive two-cycles are the first nontrivial periodic behavior in a fixed-point-free interval map. An exact sharp multiplicity bound plus an open set of coexisting locally attracting period-two cycles exposes an intrinsic nonchaotic mechanism in the motivating chaos-generation family, answering a natural parameter-wide mathematical question not settled by Lyapunov color plots. The result supplies coexistence and its sharp upper ceiling without claiming higher-period or cryptographic theorems.
